speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On the ground, we have heard recurring feedback from families and these are not just families with persons with disabilities, but also with seniors who, for some reason, have lost some of their capacities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My Parliamentary Question arises from all these recurring feedback.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There were two sets of issues normally cited.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Despite what the Minister of State mentioned that OPG has been doing.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The first set is around the difficulties when they apply for deputyship.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Usually, many of these families have limited access to knowledge and guidance, they do not even know where to go.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Despite a simplified process, it is actually not so simple.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Most applicants, especially those who are not so educated or not so proficient in English, do require hands-on guidance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And without it, the process is quite daunting.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Also, for deputyship, unlike the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), it is more costly and administratively burdensome as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are also difficulties after deputyship orders are made.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Like the Minister of State mentioned, the annual report; it is not so easy for people to even fill up.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some of my volunteers, including lawyers who help them, find it is not so straightforward for those post deputyship burdens —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Phua, do you want to ask your supplementary question?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And then, make the information available for them.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I believe the Member can appreciate that the scope of responsibility required of a deputy is much broader.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The Member made comparisons to the LPA process.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Indeed, for deputies, they do have to exercise quite a lot more responsibilities and these can vary quite widely depending on what the Court decides upon.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Having said so, I acknowledge the comments and feedback from the Member.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: It is especially problematic when it comes to having to deal with amounts of those who have lost mental capacity and the amounts may not be a lot of money, but you need it for sustenance or maybe to settle some debts or some payments, particularly of caregivers, relatives, friends, even neighbours.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Because now, increasingly, you have cases of dementia.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We may be doing a lot of efforts at LPAs, but there are those who fall outside of it.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This is a suggestion for MSF to look at, but can we set some thresholds with banks and financial institutions where we are able to withdraw those monies to pay for simple bills, rather than be in debt which then rolls on?
